Build a Todo app in a single self-contained HTML file. Requirements:
- Add new todos
- Mark todos as complete (strikethrough)
- Delete todos
- Filter: All / Active / Completed
- Persist to localStorage

Deliver only the HTML file with JS, CSS, HTML. Use file name "todo_openrouter-moonshotai-kimi-k3_01.html"

{"path": "todo_openrouter-moonshotai-kimi-k3_01.html", "edit_description": "Create a new single self-contained HTML file implementing a complete Todo app. All CSS must be in a <style> block in <head> and all JS in a <script> block at the end of <body> — no external resources.

Functional requirements (all mandatory):
1. Add new todos: an input field + "Add" button; pressing Enter in the input also adds. Trim whitespace; ignore empty input. Clear input after adding.
2. Mark todos as complete: each todo item has a checkbox (or click on the item) that toggles completed state; completed todos show strikethrough text and dimmed color.
3. Delete todos: each item has a delete (×) button that removes it.
4. Filters: three buttons "All" / "Active" / "Completed" that filter the visible list; the active filter button is visually highlighted.
5. Persist to localStorage: save the todo list (array of {id, text, completed}) under a key like 'todos' on every change; load and render on page load.
6. Show a footer with count of remaining active items (e.g. "3 items left"). Show an empty-state message when the current filter has no todos.

Implementation details:
- Use vanilla JS with a render() function that re-renders the list from the state array; use crypto.randomUUID() or Date.now()+Math.random() for ids.
- Use event delegation or per-item listeners; make sure XSS-safe rendering (use textContent, not innerHTML, for todo text).
- Modern, clean, responsive design: centered card layout (max-width ~500px), pleasant color scheme, subtle shadows, rounded corners, hover effects on buttons, smooth transitions. Works on mobile widths.
- Include a visible <h1> title like "Todo App".
- Include proper <!DOCTYPE html>, <html lang="en">, meta charset and viewport tags."}
